documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

Angela is a 34 y/o elementary school teacher establishing care with us. Her old PCP was across the river and she wanted somewhere she could actually reach by text. Main issue today is a cough.

HPI: Caught a cold around the first week of July (stuffy nose, sore throat, a few days of feeling run down). The cold itself cleared without anything but the cough never left, now about 3 weeks. Much worse once she lies down at night. Describes a constant feeling of mucus running down the back of her throat and having to clear it all day, which is not great when she's trying to run summer reading groups. Has been through two different drugstore cough syrups without any benefit. No fever now, no shortness of breath, no wheeze, no chest pain. No heartburn symptoms she can identify.

PMH: Nothing significant. Never had asthma or any lung problem.
PSH: None.
Meds: None. No supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family hx: Nothing significant that she knows of.
Social: Teaches 2nd grade. Never smoked, no vaping. Drinks socially, a glass of wine or two a week. Lives in Northampton.

Exam: Vitals reviewed and normal. Well appearing, clears her throat a few times during the visit. Ears and nose normal. Oropharynx clear. No cervical adenopathy, thyroid not enlarged. Lungs clear throughout, no wheezes, rales or rhonchi. Heart regular, no murmur. Rest of exam unremarkable.

A/P:
1. Upper airway cough syndrome (postnasal drip) after a viral URI. Clear lungs, no red flags, nonsmoker. Discussed that this usually fades over a few more weeks as the upper airway settles down. Return or message if it is not clearly better in 3-4 weeks, or sooner with fever, shortness of breath or blood in sputum.
2. Health maintenance: will request records from her prior office to see what screening is up to date. Would like a full physical in the fall once school is back in.

RTC: physical in the fall, sooner prn.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

Came in before school, fasting. Feels well. The summer cough cleared in mid-August and has not come back. No new concerns. Sleep ok, busy start to the school year. Periods regular. 
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, wine 1-2/wk, no other substances.
PHQ-2: 0.

ROS: negative in full.

Exam: vitals reviewed, normal. Pleasant, well appearing. HEENT unremarkable, oropharynx clear. Neck supple, thyroid normal size and nontender, no nodes. Lungs clear. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without concerning lesions. Extremities without edema. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P:
1. Adult health maintenance, age 34.
 - Cervical: co-test 03/2023 normal per outside records, next due 2028.
 - Fasting labs today: CBC, CMP, lipids. One-time HIV and hep C screening, she agrees.
 - Flu and updated COVID vaccines given today. Tdap current (2021).
 - Sunscreen, seat belts, the usual.
2. Upper airway cough syndrome, resolved. Off the problem list.

Follow up in a year, or sooner prn. Will message results.

documents.title: Immunization Administration
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Screening questions reviewed, no contraindications. Influenza vaccine 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. Pfizer COVID-19 2025-26 formula 0.3 mL IM left deltoid. VIS given for both. Tolerated well, waited 15 min without issue.

documents.title: Your Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Angela - everything from Wednesday came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar, and cholesterol all look good, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. See you next fall.

documents.title: Sore neck and racing heart
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning. For about a week the front of my neck has been sore and it feels full, like something is pressing when I swallow. I've been running low fevers on and off, feel wiped out, and my heart keeps racing and pounding even sitting at my desk. I also keep breaking into sweats. I had a cold a couple of weeks ago that went away on its own. Can I be seen? I can leave school early.

documents.title: RE: Sore neck and racing heart
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, please come in today. I have 3:30 open. If the racing comes with chest pain, fainting or trouble breathing before then, go to the ED.

events.reason: Anterior neck pain, low-grade fevers, palpitations

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Same-Day Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
SAME-DAY VISIT

S: ~1 week of anterior neck pain and a sense of fullness in the throat, worse when she swallows or turns her head. Low-grade fevers at home, malaise, episodes of palpitations at rest, and intermittent sweats. Had a cold roughly two weeks ago that cleared without treatment. No chest pain, no syncope, no dyspnea. No meds, nothing new OTC. NKDA.

O: T 37.9. Other vitals per flowsheet. Looks tired but not toxic. Oropharynx clear. Thyroid enlarged and distinctly tender to palpation, no discrete nodule felt. No cervical lymphadenopathy. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. No tremor appreciated.

A/P:
Tender, enlarged thyroid with fever and hyperadrenergic symptoms after a viral illness. Concerned for an inflammatory thyroiditis. TSH, free T4, ESR, CRP drawn today. Will call her tomorrow with results and arrange endocrinology. ED precautions reviewed.

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 04/29/2026
Re: Angela Damon, DOB 05/18/1991
Referred by: primary care

Thank you for sending Ms. Damon, a 34 year old elementary school teacher, for evaluation of a painful thyroid.

History: For two weeks she has had pain at the front of the neck with a sense of throat fullness, along with low-grade fevers and general malaise. She describes palpitations and intermittent sweating. About three weeks ago she had an upper respiratory infection that resolved without any treatment. She was seen in primary care in 2025 for a post-viral cough, since resolved, and has otherwise been healthy.

Past surgical history: none.
Medications: none.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: noncontributory.
Social history: never smoker; alcohol socially, 1-2 drinks per week; teaches elementary school.

Examination: HR 88, BP 132/85. Alert, mildly anxious, in no distress. The thyroid is diffusely enlarged and tender to light palpation, without nodularity. No cervical adenopathy. Lungs clear, heart regular. Skin warm.

Data (drawn 04/21/2026 by primary care): TSH <0.01 mIU/L, free T4 2.5 ng/dL, ESR 70 mm/hr, CRP 8 mg/L.

Assessment: Subacute (granulomatous) thyroiditis. The painful, tender gland following a viral illness, with thyrotoxic labs and a markedly elevated sedimentation rate, makes this the diagnosis.

Plan:
1. Reviewed the expected course with her: the thyroid releases stored hormone for several weeks, and most people recover normal function over the following months.
2. Repeat TSH and free T4 in about 6 weeks; these can be drawn through her primary care office with a copy to us.
3. She should call for worsening neck pain, high fever, or palpitations that are not settling.
4. Follow up here as needed depending on the repeat labs.

Thank you for involving us in her care.

Endocrinology
